source.author: verg
source.text: effigies sacrae divom Phrygiique Penates, quos mecum a Troia mediisque ex ignibus urbis extuleram, visi ante oculos astare iacentis in somnis, multo manifesti lumine, qua se plena per insertas fundebat luna fenestras; tum sic affari et curas his demere dictis:
source.text_original: effigies sacrae divom Phrygiique Penates, / quos mecum a Troia mediisque ex ignibus urbis / extuleram, visi ante oculos astare iacentis / in somnis, multo manifesti lumine, qua se / plena per insertas fundebat luna fenestras; / tum sic affari et curas his demere dictis: /
source.text_english: Images of the holy gods and the Phrygian Penates, whom I had carried off with me from Troy and from the midst of the city’s fires, seemed in my sleep to stand before the eyes of me as I lay there, plain to see in a great light, as the full moon poured itself through the open windows; then thus to address me and to relieve my cares with these words:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_original: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, / hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque / visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni / silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_english: But those in whom there is a passion for the fields and for the guiltless plough, these are spurred on; and, as they are seen, they sing of the raft through the years and roads with great praise, in clear light, along with Fauni, the goddesses of the woods, and the Rivers with uplifted horns.
